full_judgment:
2. The short fact of the case is, that pre-emptor-respondent-opposite party No. 1 filed the above pre-emption case against the pre-emptee petitioner and others for getting an order for pre-emption on 12-2-1996 in respect of the case land of Mouza Dhania appertaining to CS Khatian No. 139, SA Khatian No. 154 in Plot No. 1409, measuring an area of land 1.16 acres out of which 0.33 acre is the case land for pre-emption. Pre-emptor further stated that he is a co-sharer in the case holding and as well as a tenant in holding, land contiguous to the case land. The further case of the pre-emptor is that one Kalimuddin, the great grandfather of the pre-emptor opposite party No. 1 was the original owner of the case holding and the CS record was prepared in sole name of Kadam Ali, the younger son of Kalimuddin. But the sons of said Kalimuddin by mutual agreement partitioned the case property and enjoying and possessing the case land holding among themselves and in consequence Sk Syed Ali transferred the case land along with other lands to one Sk Nizam Uddin, the father of the petitioner by a deed of gift dated 27-3-1954. The SA Khatian in respect of 1.00 acre of land out of the total case land was prepared in the name of Salim Meah and others and SA Khatian No. 155 for the rest portion of the case land was prepared in the name of the heirs of Kadam Ali. But when the recent RS record was prepared the case land was recorded correctly in the name of the father of the pre-emptor opposite party No. 1. The pre-emptor of the case land obtained the land from his father by way of Heba-bil-Ewaj dated 4-1-1978 and he was also owner and possessor of the land in Plot Nos. 1412 and 1413 contiguous to the case land. The seller opposite party No. 2 sold out the case land to the preempted-petitioner Nos. 1-3 behind the back of the pre-emptor without serving any notice upon the heirs including the pre-emptor about 21/2 months ago and the opposite party No. 2 disclosed to the locality that she sold out the case land. Thereafter, he on search obtained the certified copy of the sale deed on 31-12-1995 and became sure about the transfer of the case land beyond his knowledge and hence the case. 

 3. The preempted-petitioners contested the case by filing written objection denying the material allegations of the pre-emption petition contending, inter alia, that the entire case land in CS Khatian jote belonged to Kadam Ali who while owning and possessing the same died leaving behind son Golam Mostafa and daughter Basirunnessa now opposite party No. 2 who sold out the case land to the pre-emptee petitioners by a registered kabala No. 5685 dated 29-8-1992 and transferred the possession of the case land to them. After the purchase the pre-empted petitioners raised the land by filling earth and then constructed semi-pica building and thereafter the opposite party Nos. 1 and 3, now petitioner Nos. 1 and 2, transferred the case land in favour of Sheikh Raisuddin, Dalilur Rahman and Nur Mohammad by a registered power of Attorney on 8-11-95. The said Attorney made further development of the case land by constructing semi-pucca house and have been residing therein peacefully. The opposite party No. 1 being allured by the increased value of the case land filed the instant case with false statement in order to grab the case land and to harass the purchaser petitioners. The pre-emptor is a stranger in the case land and did not sell the property secretly to the preempted. The petitioners' case is false and hence the Miscellaneous Case is liable to be dismissed with cost. 

 4. During the course of hearing of the case pre-emptor examined two witnesses and, on the other hand, opposite party pre-emptee examined as many as three witnesses in this case. Pre-emptor Sk Md Tajuddin was examined as PW 1 who categorically stated that originally Kadam Ali, son of Kalimuddin, was the owner and possessor of the case land measuring 1.16 acres of land in CS Khatian No. 139, Kalimuddin had four sons namely, Mainuddin, Samaruddin, Syed Ali and Kadam Ali, they were possessing and enjoying the property by amicable partition. The pre-emptor Tajuddin was the grandson of Sk Syed All who is a co-sharer by inheritance. During the RS settlement operation the name of four brothers i.e. Mainuddin, Samaruddin, Sk Syed Ali and Kadam Ali were rightly recorded in Khatian No. 391 measuring 16 decimals in the name of Golam Mostafa, Abed Ali and Bashirunnessa, sons and one daughter of Kadam Ali and bearing Khatian No. 417 measuring one acre in the name of heirs of Mainuddin, Samaruddin and Syed Ali. The PW 1 exhibited both the RS Khatian as exhibit 6 series and also exhibited the CS Khatians as Exhibit 1. The pre-emptor-petitioner further stated in his evidence that pre-emptee-opposite party secretly purchased 33 decimals of land from Bashirunnessa, daughter of Kadam Ali in CS Plot No. 1409. The PW 1 further stated that he was the owner and possessor of CS Plot Nos. 1412 and 1413 which were contiguous to CS Plot No. 1409, as such, the pre-emptor was co-sharer by inheritance and also owner and possessor of land contiguous to case land. He also stated in his evidence that the pre-emptee-opposite party is a stranger and also stated that he was absolutely ignorant about the sale of the case property and subsequently, in the locality seller Bashirunnessa disclosed that she had sold out the case land to the preempted-opposite party. 

 12. On the other hand, the learned Counsel Mr SRM Lutfor Rahman Akhand, appearing on behalf of the pre-emptor-petitioner respondent-opposite party, submits that the learned trial Court as well as the lower appellate Court after discussing the evidence on record and also considering the exhibits, documents and other connected papers and the facts and circumstances of the case, passed the judgment and order which is absolutely justified and there is no legal infirmity nor the courts below acted illegally in passing the judgment and order in favour of the pre-emptor-petitioner. The pre-emptor-petitioner Tajuddin examined two witnesses including himself, Tajuddin, as PW 1 who categorically stated that he was a co-sharer by inheritance and also he has got contiguous land situated with the case land. He further disclosed in his evidence that while the case land was sold out no notice was served under section 89 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. He also stated that he was absolutely in the dark about the transfer of the land and long after while Bashir-un-nessa after 3 and a half year disclosed in the locality that she sold 33 decimals of land to the pre-emptee-opposite parties then he came to know. Thereafter, he rushed to the Sub-Registrar Office and obtained the certified copy of the sale deed to become sure about the transfer of the land. He further disclosed in his evidence that the pre-emptor-petitioner was in the possession of the suit property. He was cross-examined by the lawyer of the adverse party but he could not be shaken in cross-examination. The learned Counsel also submits that the pre-emptor-petitioner exhibited CS Khatian as exhibit-1 and RS Khatian as exhibit-6 showing that petitioner was a co-sharer by inheritance. Next he submits that the lower appellate Court elaborately discussed the evidence on record, also the exhibits and documents and came to a correct finding and observation in his judgment that admittedly the pre-emptor-petitioner was not served with any notice of the transfer of the case land as required under section 89(4) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, which was required to be served upon him in the status of his being a co-sharer of the case holding and, as such, he filed the pre-emption Miscellaneous Case within 4(four) months from the date of his knowledge of the transfer under the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. The learned Counsel finally submits that since both the courts below committed no error and illegality in finding of the facts and circumstances of the case it should not be interfered by this court.
